item.title: 3 quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s win over Delaware: This team is going to have some growing pains
item.description: Eian Elmer #55 of the Wisconsin Badgers dribbles the basketball while being defended by Kam Martin #2 of the Denver Pioneers at Kohl Center in Madison, Wisconsin, on November 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers beat the Delaware Blue Hens 73-64 on Friday to improve to 2-0, just days after beating the Denver Pioneers 75-68 in their season opener on Monday. Now, Monday’s game was more of a struggle for the Badgers, with things getting within single digits in the final minutes. This game wasn’t as close as the score implied at the end, with Wisconsin holding a comfortable double-digit lead for most of the last seven minutes. But the Badgers look like a major work in progress through two games, as they sort things out with their new-look roster. Here are three quick takeaways from Wisconsin’s 73-64 win over Delaware on Friday evening. Offense too stagnant early The Badgers got off to this one shooting a ton of threes, with Braeden Carrington, Nolan Winter, and Eian Elmer all connecting from deep. But as the first half went along and Delaware kept things close, the Badgers became far too stagnant on offense. While the ball was moving around, Wisconsin did not attack the basket until late in the shot clock, instead passing around the perimeter looking for threes. It was far too passive an outlook, while Delaware was looking to be aggressive and take the game to Wisconsin on the other end. Owen Foxwell was the only one initiating by attacking, and those actions alone set up a couple of open shots and looks at the rim. Foxwell had four assists, but could not get his rhythm as a scorer, going 1 for 5 from the field, while splitting his lone pair of free throws. In the second half, we saw Foxwell attack more and end up with 13 points in the half alone, working well from the free-throw line. But as a team, that has to be more consistently happening to set up the threes, not the other way around. This could also be partly because of a new group of players settling in together. Guys are still figuring out their spots and with that has been some passive play to start the season. Eian Elmer’s aggressiveness Eian Elmer is going to be a big part of this team’s success this year. The Badgers are going to need him to step up and potentially take over as their top scorer, with Foxwell being their top facilitator. He had 18 points on 13 shots in the opener, and I thought there were times he was too hesitant in this one after popping a few early threes. Elmer took a poor three later in the first half from too deep, and all of his field goal makes were from beyond the arc on Friday. The Badgers need more initiators alongside Foxwell, and Elmer is the guy who’s going to have to step up from that group. He had 11 points in Friday’s win, shooting 3 of 8 from the field and 3 of 6 from deep, while adding four rebounds and two blocks. item.title: Saban Slams 24-Team Playoff, Says It’s “Too Many”
item.description: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Nick Saban talks to the media at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Nick Saban cut right through the noise on Friday when he called the new 24-team playoff a bad idea . The former Alabama coach told fans on the “New Heights” podcast that the field is simply too crowded. He believes the expansion hurts the game more than it helps. Saban made his point clear while talking to the Kelce brothers about the changes coming next season. The core issue is that the best teams will still win, but the rest will just play for cash. Saban argued that the current system already stretched players too thin with extra games. He noted that his teams played 15 games three times and he thought that was too many, according to Yahoo Sports . Now the plan adds even more pressure without fixing the quality of the competition. Money Is The Only Reason When Travis Kelce asked Saban why anyone would push for a bigger tournament, the answer was blunt. “So what is the reason to actually do it?” Saban asked the audience on the Friday podcast. Jason Kelce answered immediately, saying, “Money.” Saban agreed with the assessment but warned fans about the cost of that cash. He hates to see the SEC championship game go away because it means so much to the players and fans. That tradition is a big thing for the league, and it is a great venue that people love. The new rules mean conference title games will likely disappear to make room for the expanded playoff. As part of the agreement, a Big Ten squad must face a power opponent in a non-conference matchup. Should conference titles remain, a team might compete in 18 contests upon advancing to the national title. Dropping the title games allows the playoffs to start earlier and caps the total number of games at 17. Saban feels this is still too much for college athletes to handle. Tradition Gets Lost For A Deal The College Football Playoff issued a statement on Friday afternoon about the media rights for this expansion. The statement said, “A formal agreement between the CFP and ESPN regarding future media rights in connection with potential expansion is in the final stages of review by the CFP.” This confirms the deal is moving forward despite the complaints from the coaching ranks. Saban thinks the system would have worked fine with just 12 or maybe 16 teams. He said the 12-team version was a good tournament even if a few teams that should not have been in got selected. The SEC already has a nine-game schedule in place to match the other power conferences. This rule forces teams to play tougher opponents without the safety net of a conference title game. Saban believes pride in winning a conference championship matters more than adding weak teams to a bracket. He thinks the political pressure to make the field bigger led to a flawed plan. The former coach knows that 24 teams are too many for a true national championship race.

item.title: CB South falls to Coatesville in district football playoff opener
item.description: WARRINGTON — As a senior captain at Central Bucks East in 2005, Johnny Cataldo and the Patriots won the Suburban One League Continental Conference championship and a District One playoff game with Chuck Rocconi and Mike Elko as co-coaches filling in for the respected Larry Greene (cancer). In 2026, with Cataldo and Bart Szarko as Central Bucks South co-coaches after the respected Tom Hetrick resigned due to a family health issue, the Titans earned a share of the SOL National with Central Bucks West and Pennridge. CB South dropped a 35-26 decision to Coatesville in a PIAA District One Class 6A first-round game Friday night at Titan Field, ending its season. The Titans had won six of their last seven regular-season games, including a victory over undefeated Pennridge , after starting the season 0-3. Sophomore running back Andre Watson had 32 carries for 229 yards rushing and two touchdowns for Coatesville. item.title: ‘Someone Tell Brittany Mahomes,’ ‘Argument Over’ — NFL Fans React to Jason, Travis Kelce Taking Refs’ Side in Controversial Call During Broncos-Chiefs
item.description: Jason Kelce, Brittany Mahomes and Travis Kelce Even with one of them in a Kansas City Chiefs uniform, Jason and Travis Kelce sided with the officials. On Wednesday’s episode of “New Heights,” the brothers agreed with the false start called on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore that wiped out Patrick Mahomes’ would-be winning touchdown pass in Week 8’s 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. However, that put the brothers on the other side of the call from Brittany Mahomes, who blasted it in an Instagram story after the game. NFL fans reacting to the clip treated the brothers’ take as the final word, with some of them also asking Patrick Mahomes’ wife to take notice. NFL Fans React as Travis and Jason Kelce Weigh In On Officiating Debate Trailing 28-24, the Chiefs drove from their own 44, and Mahomes’ 1-yard touchdown throw to Rashee Rice looked like the winner until Moore’s flag erased it. On the replay, Moore’s hips shift slightly as he turns his head toward Mahomes. At the same instant, right guard Trey Smith, who had been looking back toward the quarterback before the snap, swings his own head forward. Pushed back 5 yards to the 6, Kansas City replayed fourth down, and Malcolm Roach’s sack of Mahomes ended the game. Brittany wrote that night: “You can’t tell me you call that on a game-winning TD, oh wait, yeah, I can, ’cause it’s us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can’t tell me otherwise.” Three days later, the Kelce brothers broke down the same play and reached a different conclusion. “I’m going to go on record and say that this is definitely a penalty,” Jason said, as Travis agreed, “Yeah, he flinches.” Fans who agreed with the officials now had the brothers’ words to point to, and Brittany’s name came up more than once. “Someone tell Brittany Mahomes,” one fan wrote. This user took aim at Chiefs fans as a whole: “After all the crying/complaining that KC fans did… Travis Kelce comes out to say 77 flinched.” Moore, the tackle at the center of the call, wears No. 77 for Kansas City. Another fan needed only three words: “Done. Argument over.” The flag on Moore was one of 11 penalties for 105 yards called against Kansas City in Denver, while the Broncos were flagged six times for 45 yards. By the count from AP’s Josh Dubow, the Chiefs have been penalized 1,100 more yards than their opponents since Mahomes took over as the starter in 2018, and only the Jets and Saints have a worse differential over that span. item.title: Jayson Tatum, Boston Celtics exterminate Charlotte Hornets, 119-80, in NBA Cup play
item.description: Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has made Charlotte into a second home, and that's not just because he played a few hours down the road at Duke University as a youngster. It's more so due to the fact that the six-time All-Star has repeatedly torched the Charlotte Hornets at the Spectrum Center. And following a 119-80 drubbing of the Hornets on Friday night, Tatum has now scored at least 30 points in three of his last four outings in the Queen City. The 2024 NBA champion recorded a game-high 34 points — 1 more than the Hornets' starters had combined — to go along with 9 assists and 8 rebounds in the blowout victory. It only took him three quarters to reach that impressive total, too, as the Celtics led by more than 30 points heading into the final frame and were able to lean on their reserves the rest of the way. Tatum aside, practically every Celtic contributed during the NBA Cup duel. Guard Derrick White finished with 18 points on 60 percent shooting, point guard Payton Pritchard added 10 points off the bench, and center Mitchell Robinson notched 7 rebounds in just 15 minutes. All of these stellar performances helped fuel the 39-point win, which is significant because point differential matters in NBA Cup play. Boston currently sits atop the East Group C standings at 2-0 and is 7-2 overall to start the 2026-27 campaign. The Celtics will look to carry that momentum on the road and into a Sunday night showdown with the struggling Milwaukee Bucks , who they recently defeated on Wednesday evening at TD Garden. item.title: Greenwich girls volleyball beats Trumbull to win second straight FCIAC championship
item.description: Greenwich celebrates winning the FCIAC volleyball championship over Trumbull at Stamford High School in Stamford on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Scott Ericson/Hearst Connecticut Media) STAMFORD - The top-seeded Greenwich girls volleyball team made it two in a row, beating No. 2 Trumbull 3-1 (25-21, 25-27, 25-22, 25-13) Friday night at Stamford High to claim back-to-back FCIAC championships. It is the fifth overall championship for the Cardinals, who remained unbeaten (20-0) heading into the CIAC tournament. "It's so exciting and such an amazing feeling, and I am so proud of my whole team," Greenwich junior libero Bailee Dayon said. "I think we set up a very great block the last two sets and it made it easier for me to read." Dayon was in fact able to read the Trumbull attack well, recording 27 digs in the match to go along with 13 assists and 15 service points, many of which came when Greenwich needed them the most. "(Dayon) is just great all the time," Greenwich coach Marianna Linnehan said. "She is fantastic. That girl can just dig every ball. When Mckenzyi (Bell of Trumbull) was in the front row, she was killing us and we really fixed that in the last two sets." For Greenwich, Kayah Armstrong had 20 kills and two blocks, Heidi Zieme had 16 digs and 14 kills, Victoria Sullivan had 15 digs and 25 assists, and Beatriz Lisboa Da Cunha De Freitas had 20 assists and nine digs. Bell was stellar all night at the net for Trumbull, delivering 17 kills. "I thought sets one through three we did exactly what we had to do, but in set four, we kind of ran out of steam a bit," Trumbull coach Nicole Trommelen said. "It was fun for a big stretch of that game watching Mckenzyi go." After splitting the first two sets, Trumbull (19-2) led most of the third until Greenwich took its first lead at 21-20. Trumbull's only loss of the regular season came to Greenwich. Those were the only two sets Greenwich dropped during the regular season in going unbeaten. item.title: UNC dominates behind Terrence Brown in win over Wofford
item.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first UNC basketball game of the season may have felt like uneasy dental work with a happy ending after the Tar Heels managed to do just enough to beat Western Carolina. Friday night against Wofford was a different story. As in their first game, the Tar Heels never trailed. What was different, though, was that the Tar Heels looked the part as they overpowered the Terriers on their way to a 109-70 win. It was the highest point total for the Tar Heels since November of 2018. Carolina’s offense definitely came easier in this one with five players ending up in double figures. Michael Malone continued his five in, five out strategy playing with an A/B lineup. Terrence Brown was very good for the A group, leading the team with 21 points. Jaydon Young, Alex Samodurov, and Maximo Adams all turned in strong performances for the B side. They finished with 15, 13, and 11 points, respectively. Adams led the team in rebounds with 11. The bench was responsible for 58 of the Tar Heels’ points. Jarin Stevenson was the other Tar Heel in double figures with 10 points. If it weren’t for the efforts of Cutter Sisk for Wofford, the final score would have been even more lopsided. He was responsible for 27 of the Terriers’ points. He was 11-18 from the field and grabbed seven boards to lead Wofford. The Terriers got the best of the Heels on the offensive glass, 17-14, but the Heels converted more second-chance points, 19-10. The overall rebounding margin was still too close for comfort with UNC holding a +7 mark in the category, but almost everything else was so lopsided that it didn’t become a major factor. The Heels shot 52% from the field and made 10 of their three-point attempts. They also converted on 23 of their 29 free throw attempts. Seven steals for the Heels helped lead to 13 turnovers for Wofford. Carolina turned those into 14 points on the other end. After a couple nail-biter exhibition game and a too-close-for-comfort start to the season, it was very good to get a comfortable win. It was also great to see that success was spread across so much of the lineup. Hopefully this was the game that gets Brown fully going, and Adams looked very impressive as a freshman playing in just his second game. Depth has not been a reliable feature at times in recent memory for Carolina, but the team showed tonight that there are more than a few guys who can step up and put points on the board. Carolina tries to keep it rolling on Tuesday when they welcome Wyoming to Chapel Hill.

item.title: FSU moves to 2-0 with 23-point win over Troy
item.description: Florida State began 2-0 for the second straight season under head coach Luke Loucks, taking down the Troy Trojans 91-68 in the Seminoles’ home opener. Marcis Ponder had a second straight double-double, with 10 points and 10 rebounds, while Shon Abaev led all scorers with 20 points. Sebastian Rancik had 18 points and three rebounds, going a perfect 8-for-8 from the charity stripe. Florida State started hot, shooting out to a 12-2 lead, but then an offensive drought saw the Seminoles stall out. FSU took its largest lead to that point at the 12:45 mark, going up 17-5 off a Kameron Taylor three, but the momentum was lost as Florida State struggled to hit anything from the field — though a strong performance on the glass helped mitigate those shooting woes. The Seminoles made just two baskets over the next eight minutes, going 2-for-14 before a Rancik three-ball. FSU proceeded to go on a 10-2 run to close out the half, pushing its lead to 14 before a late three from Troy made it a 37-26 game at the close of the first. item.title: Wei Lin leads Oregon men's basketball's rout of Eastern Washington
item.description: The strength of the Oregon men’s basketball team will be its depth and its roster of interchangeable parts, interim coach Tony Stubblefield has declared on several occasions the past month. On Nov. 6, it was Wei Lin’s turn to claim the spotlight. The junior reserve point guard, one of just two returning players for the Ducks, had 20 points to lead Oregon to a 98-71 nonconference rout of Eastern Washington on Friday afternoon in Matthew Knight Arena. Lin's point total was his second highest in 32 games at Oregon (2-0) and three points shy of his career high – a 23-point performance in overtime against Rutgers last season. “He really provided a big spark for us off the bench,” Stubblefield said. Lin finished 7 for 9 from the field, 3 for 5 from 3-point range, and had four rebounds, three steals and just two turnovers in 21 minutes. One of his turnovers was the result of an errant behind-the-back-pass attempt on a fast break Lin started with a steal late in the second half. “Wei has really put in the work,” Stubblefield said. “He’s very coachable and it looks like he’s gotten better from last year. He’s defending harder and being more of an all-around basketball player. … And he’s taking better shots." Lin wasn’t the only Duck to impress on offense. Fred Payne had 16 points and was 4 for 6 from 3-point range, Pharoah Compton scored 13 and was 6 for 6 from the field and Malique Ewin had 10 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. Oregon shot 60% from the field (39 for 65) for the second game in a row, had 26 assists and won the rebounding battle 38-24. The Ducks were up 53-39 at halftime and only trailed for 22 seconds the entire game. And just like in their season-opening win against Montana last Monday, the Ducks entertained with their athleticism and ability to play above the rim, especially on the fast break. “During the recruiting process, that was something we really looked for,” Stubblefield said. “Getting back to our athleticism, improving our athleticism. So we had a good idea what we were getting with these young men, but they’ve been great to work with.” Oregon will be without guard Tyrone Riley IV until December Oregon played Friday without junior guard Tyrone Riley IV, who sustained a left hand injury against Montana and will be out for at least four weeks. He was on the bench Friday with a wrap on his thumb. The transfer from San Francisco had a team-high 17 points against the Grizzlies, along with four steals, three assists and two blocks. Stubblefield called it a "fluke injury" and added that "we got guys over there that are ready to step up and we'll be OK until he gets back." Jasper Johnson replaced him in the starting lineup against Eastern Washington and had six points, one assist and four turnovers. What’s next for Oregon men’s basketball? item.title: ‘This is sad’: Criticism mounts as Dianna Russini makes media return after Mike Vrabel scandal
item.description: Dianna Russini Dianna Russini appears to be on the verge of returning to NFL media. Her new home, however, has raised plenty of eyebrows. The former NFL insider is reportedly set to host a new weekly show with BetUS, an offshore sportsbook based in Costa Rica. Many people on social media weren’t sure what to make of that choice, especially considering the NFL’s stance on unregulated gambling. Russini’s reported return Russini resigned from her role as a senior NFL insider at The Athletic in April after photos surfaced that suggested a years-long romantic relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Both denied any wrongdoing, though The Athletic later released an internal review that called the relationship a “clear violation” of its standards. Now, it appears that Russini has found her next gig. Front Office Sports reported that she was likely to launch a digital show sponsored by a sportsbook, with BetUS emerging as the frontrunner, according to Ryan Glasspiegel, Mark Maske, and Michael McCarthy . BetUS has since teased the arrival of “a familiar voice” for a live weekly NFL show that will debut on Wednesday, Nov. 11, per Awful Announcing’s Sean Keeley . The show will reportedly feature game previews, guest interviews, and betting picks, and the host will also write a weekly column. The company plans to reveal the host on Monday, but an X account called “Russini Report” had already been promoting a live NFL show on Wednesdays. That page previously said the show was “powered by BetUS,” before the wording was removed, according to FOS. As Awful Announcing’s Brendon Kleen noted , the show will be a major test of whether Russini can still break news and draw an audience following the Vrabel scandal. Reactions Plenty of people, including some who cover the sports betting industry, questioned whether partnering with an offshore sportsbook was the right move for Russini. “For someone who has so carefully calibrated her reemergence, partnering with an offshore sportsbook while trying to rebuild NFL ties is a curious choice. The league has made its hostility to unregulated sports gambling abundantly clear. See league’s stance on prediction markets,” wrote sports betting attorney Daniel Wallach . “Over/Under on the % of people who don’t know that BetUS is an offshore sports book … 90%?” wrote Matt Perrault , host of The Bostonian vs. The Book . “Chat, is working for an offshore sportsbook a step up from being caught f***ing your interview subjects?” wrote sports betting reporter Sam McQuillan . “Russini does not have good people in her corner.
